title: optimize()/fit()/propose() with estimator=None on a one-shot iterator silently returns IgnoredDistribution(PointMass(None)) that scores every observation -inf
surface: mixle.inference.optimize / mixle.inference.fit / mixle.propose, data = generator, iter(list), map(), zip(); default structure='auto'
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np, mixle; from mixle.inference import optimize, fit; xs=[float(v) for v in np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200)]; m=optimize(iter(xs), max_its=3); print(m, m.log_density(xs[0])); print(fit(v for v in xs)); print(mixle.propose(iter(xs)).fitted); print(optimize(iter(xs), max_its=3, structure='off')); print(optimize(xs, max_its=3))"
expected: The same GaussianDistribution(0.0709, 1.0433) that optimize(xs) returns (or a ValueError). mixle.utils.automatic.profiling.normalize_input's docstring promises one-shot iterators are materialized 'because ... a one-shot iterator would silently fit a wrong/empty model on the second pass'.
observed: optimize(iter(xs)) -> IgnoredDistribution(PointMassDistribution(None)); .log_density(xs[0]) -> -inf; fit(generator) -> same; propose(iter(xs)).fitted -> None. No warning, no error. With structure='off' or an explicit estimator the fit is correct.
notes: Cause: optimize() front door (estimation.py ~1585-1610) calls _maybe_structured_model(structure_rows=data) which does rows = list(data) on the raw iterator (estimation.py:229), exhausting it; when structure inference declines, the fallback re-profiles the exhausted iterator (normalize_input -> []) and get_estimator([]) yields the empty-corpus IgnoredDistribution. Worst finding of this pass: a silent wrong model on an input type the library documents as supported.

title: RecordEstimator with aliased fields field(name, source) cannot be fit from a DataFrame through optimize()/fit(); rows are keyed by logical names but the record encoder demands source keys
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np, pandas as pd; from mixle.inference import optimize; from mixle.stats import GaussianEstimator, CategoricalEstimator; from mixle.stats.combinator.record import RecordEstimator, field; xs=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200)); df=pd.DataFrame({'x':xs,'k':['a','b']*100}); est=RecordEstimator([field('mean','x'),field('kind','k')],[GaussianEstimator(),CategoricalEstimator()]); m=optimize(df, est, fields=['x','k'], max_its=3); print(m.log_density({'x':0.1,'k':'a'}), m.log_density({'mean':0.1,'kind':'a'})); print(optimize(df, est, max_its=3))"
expected: optimize(df, est) fits a RecordDistribution({'mean':..., 'kind':...}) reading columns x and k (that is what field(name, source) is documented to do, and what seq_encode_dataframe(df, estimator=est) already does by passing _dict_keys='source').
observed: optimize(df, est) and fit(df, est) raise ValueError: record observation at row 0 must contain exactly the configured sources; missing=['x','k'], extra=['mean','kind']. Same with fields=[('mean','x'),('kind','k')]. Only fields=['x','k'] works. The fitted model then silently scores a logically-keyed row {'mean':..,'kind':..} at -inf instead of raising.
notes: _data_records_for_encoding (estimation.py:410-453) calls dataframe_records(..., as_dict=True) with the default _dict_keys='logical'; seq_encode_dataframe passes _dict_keys='source' with a comment explaining exactly this contract. The two entry points disagree.

title: A DataFrame with 2-level MultiIndex columns (or a flat Index of 2-tuples) is misparsed: each (a, b) column label is read as a (name, source) field spec
surface: mixle.data.dataframe_records / optimize(df) / propose(df) with pd.MultiIndex columns of exactly two levels
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np, pandas as pd, mixle; from mixle.inference import optimize; df=pd.DataFrame({'x':np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200),'k':['a','b']*100}); mi=df.copy(); mi.columns=pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([('num','x'),('cat','k')]); print(optimize(mi, max_its=3))"  # KeyError. Then with [('num','x'),('num','k')] -> 'logical fields must be unique'. With a 3-level MultiIndex it fits.
expected: Either fit the two columns (3-level MultiIndex columns and integer column names both work) or a ContractError naming MultiIndex columns.
observed: KeyError: 'DataFrame is missing fields: x, k' (the second tuple element is looked up as a source column); with a shared first level: ValueError: logical fields must be unique, got ['num','num']. propose(mi) fails identically.
notes: pandas_source._field_source/_field_name treat any 2-tuple as (name, source); dataframe_records feeds df.columns straight through that parser when fields is None. Only the 2-level case is affected.

title: A closed MPEncodedData handle silently yields a default/degenerate model and zero log-density instead of raising
surface: mixle.utils.parallel.multiprocessing.MPEncodedData after close(); optimize(None, est, enc_data=handle); seq_log_density_sum(handle, model)
reproduction:
PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; printf 'import numpy as np
from mixle.inference import optimize
from mixle.stats import GaussianEstimator, seq_log_density_sum
from mixle.utils.parallel.multiprocessing import MPEncodedData
if __name__=="__main__":
    xs=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200))
    h=MPEncodedData(xs, estimator=GaussianEstimator(), num_workers=2); h.close()
    print(len(h)); print(optimize(None, GaussianEstimator(), enc_data=h, max_its=3)); print(seq_log_density_sum(h, optimize(xs, GaussianEstimator())))
' > closed_mp.py; $PY closed_mp.py
expected: RuntimeError/ValueError stating the handle is closed (the class is a context manager and close() is documented as the shutdown).
observed: len(h) -> 200; optimize(None, ..., enc_data=h) -> GaussianDistribution(0.0, 1e-08) with no warning; seq_log_density_sum(h, model) -> (0, 0).
notes: close() -> _terminate_workers() empties _conns/_procs; _broadcast_collect then iterates zero connections and returns [], _fold_stats folds nothing (nobs=0) and estimator.estimate(0, ...) returns the default model, while __len__ still reports the pre-close size. A mixture estimator gives MixtureDistribution([Gaussian(0,1e-8), Gaussian(0,1e-8)],[0.5,0.5]).

title: optimize()/fit() with estimator=None reject a mixle DataSource (MaterializedSource/LazySource) with TypeError 'not iterable', although normalize_input and the explicit-estimator path accept it
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.inference import optimize; from mixle.data import as_source; from mixle.stats import GaussianEstimator; xs=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200)); print(optimize(as_source(xs), GaussianEstimator(), max_its=3)); print(optimize(as_source(xs), max_its=3, structure='off')); print(optimize(as_source(xs), max_its=3))"
expected: The same GaussianDistribution the other two calls return (mixle.data.core's docstring: a DataSource 'yields encoder-ready records' and normalize_input explicitly unwraps a DataSource).
observed: TypeError: 'MaterializedSource' object is not iterable (from estimation.py:229, _maybe_structured_model: rows = list(data)). Same for LazySource.
notes: Same root cause as P06-F01 (the structure='auto' front door iterates raw data without going through normalize_input), but here it fails loudly rather than silently.

title: numpy masked array: the auto-inference path crashes with TypeError before the dedicated masked-array guard runs
expected: Both calls raise the guard's ValueError ('optimize() received a numpy masked array with 20 masked value(s)... Pass data.compressed() ...').
observed: With GaussianEstimator: the intended ValueError. With estimator=None: TypeError: len() of unsized object from profiling._positional_row_widths (masked scalar rows).
notes: _reject_masked_data is called at estimation.py:1715, after _coerce_estimator/get_estimator has already run on the masked array.

title: numpy structured/record arrays crash the profiler with 'unhashable type: writeable void-scalar', although normalize_input's own code says structured arrays are handled
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.inference import optimize; sa=np.array([(1.0,'a'),(2.0,'b')]*50, dtype=[('x','f8'),('k','U1')]); optimize(sa, max_its=2)"
expected: A CompositeDistribution over (x, k) equivalent to optimize(sa.tolist()), or a ContractError saying structured arrays are unsupported.
observed: TypeError: unhashable type: 'writeable void-scalar' at profiling.py:2246 (DatumNode.add_datum: self.vdict[x] += 1).
notes: profiling.normalize_input returns an ndarray unchanged with the comment 'numeric/structured array: nothing to freeze', so the structured case reaches the profiler as np.void rows.

title: A column vector (n,1) with an explicit GaussianEstimator crashes inside seq_update, although the same (n,1) array encodes and scores correctly against a fitted Gaussian
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.inference import optimize; from mixle.stats import GaussianEstimator, seq_encode; x=np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200); col=x.reshape(-1,1); g=optimize(x, GaussianEstimator()); print(float(np.sum(g.seq_log_density(seq_encode(col, model=g)[0][1])))); print(type(optimize(col, max_its=2)).__name__); optimize(col, GaussianEstimator())"
expected: Either the encoder rejects (n,1) consistently at encode time with a ContractError, or the fit accepts what scoring accepts.
observed: Scoring (n,1) works (-288.027, identical to the 1-D case); auto-inference reads (n,1) as a SequenceDistribution of length-1 sequences; optimize(col, GaussianEstimator()) raises ValueError: shapes (200,1) and (200,) not aligned from gaussian.py:807 (np.dot(x, weights)).
notes: The encoder passes the 2-D array through; the accumulator assumes 1-D.

title: Several malformed inputs surface raw TypeError/RecursionError/AttributeError/numpy messages instead of the row-numbered ContractError the neighbouring paths produce
expected: A ContractError/ValueError naming the input problem (as BradleyTerry, PlackettLuce, and the empty-data/masked-array guards already do).
observed: (a) np.matrix input -> RecursionError (profiling.add_datum recurses on np.matrix rows); (b) numpy timedelta64 array -> TypeError int() ... not 'datetime.timedelta' (a pandas timedelta column fits fine); (c) 0-d array with an estimator -> TypeError len() of unsized object; (d) bytes object -> 'Integer-categorical observations must be finite exact integers'; (e) DataFrame with a duplicated column name selected via fields=['x'] -> AttributeError: 'DataFrame' object has no attribute 'tolist', and without fields -> 'logical fields must be unique' which does not mention duplicate column names; (f) ThurstoneMostellerEstimator with a None row -> TypeError 'NoneType' object is not iterable, whereas BradleyTerryEstimator on the same data says 'row 50 has no items ...'; (g) MallowsEstimator with a ragged ranking -> numpy's 'inhomogeneous shape' message, whereas PlackettLuce says 'full Plackett-Luce rankings must all have length 4'.
notes: Item (g) is the same defect class the 0.8.1 changelog says was fixed for mixed 2-/3-tuple paired comparisons ('instead of numpy's inhomogeneous shape message'); the Mallows encoder was not covered.

title: A mapping of columns ({'x': [...], 'k': [...]}) is silently fit as a categorical over the column NAMES; describe() on it says 'no catalogued capability detected' and propose(...).fitted is None
surface: optimize(dict_of_columns), mixle.describe(dict), mixle.propose(dict); also optimize('a string') fits a categorical over characters
reproduction: PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; $PY -c "import numpy as np, mixle; from mixle.inference import optimize; xs=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(size=200)); d={'x':xs,'k':['a','b']*100}; print(optimize(d, max_its=2)); print(mixle.describe(d)); print(mixle.propose(d).fitted); print(optimize('hello world', max_its=2))"
expected: Either a per-column model (a dict of equal-length columns is the canonical pd.DataFrame constructor input) or a ContractError saying a mapping of columns is not a record sequence. The 0.8.1 changelog says describe() on raw data now points at propose().
observed: optimize(d) -> CategoricalDistribution({'k': 0.5, 'x': 0.5}) with no warning; describe(d) -> 'dict — no catalogued capability detected'; propose(d).fitted -> None; optimize('hello world') -> CategoricalDistribution over 9 characters.
notes: Plain Python iteration semantics, but a silent wrong model on a very common shape of tabular input.

title: backend='mp' accepts num_workers far above the core count, spawns them all, and fails only after the setup timeout (about 6.5 minutes for 1000 workers on a 10-core machine)
surface: optimize(data, est, backend='mp', num_workers=1000) with 20000 observations; MPEncodedData.__init__
reproduction:
PY=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/.ci-repro-colima/candidate-081/venv/bin/python; cd /tmp; printf 'from mixle.inference import optimize
from mixle.stats import *
if __name__=="__main__":
    truth=CompositeDistribution((GaussianDistribution(2.0,1.5),CategoricalDistribution({"a":0.6,"b":0.3,"c":0.1}),PoissonDistribution(4.0)))
    data=truth.sampler(1).sample(20000)
    est=CompositeEstimator((GaussianEstimator(),CategoricalEstimator(),PoissonEstimator()))
    print(optimize(data, est, max_its=1, backend="mp", num_workers=1000))
' > mp1000.py; time $PY mp1000.py
expected: Either a cap at a sane multiple of cpu_count (the docstring says the default is 'CPU count, capped at the number of observations') or a prompt ValueError.
observed: 384.7 s wall, 1000 spawned processes, then TimeoutError: parallel worker 122 timed out after 30.000s during setup; stray 'Process SpawnProcess-N:' tracebacks on stderr. num_workers=0, -1, 2.5 and '4' are silently accepted and coerced.
notes: Not a hang: it terminates and cleans up its workers. Recorded as docs because explicit oversubscription is caller error, but the failure mode is slow and the docstring does not say explicit values are only capped at n.
